questions.question: A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on an item. What is the final price of an item marked at ₹1000?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on an item. What is the final price of an item marked at ₹1000?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1000

First Discount = 20%

Second Discount = 10%

Formula used:

Final Price = MP × (1 - First Discount/100) × (1 - Second Discount/100)

Calculations:

Final Price = ₹1000 × (1 - 20/100) × (1 - 10/100)

⇒ Final Price = ₹1000 × 0.8 × 0.9

⇒ Final Price = ₹720

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

questions.question: An item has a cost price of 1000. A merchant sets the marked price at 1200 and offers a discount of 40 percent. What is the merchant's profit or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: An item has a cost price of 1000. A merchant sets the marked price at 1200 and offers a discount of 40 percent. What is the merchant's profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the effective ratio method: Selling Price (SP) / Cost Price (CP) = (MP / CP) × (100 − D)% / 100.

Ratio SP / CP = (1200 / 1000) × (60 / 100) = 1.2 × 0.6 = 0.72.

Since the ratio is less than 1, it is a Loss of (1 − 0.72) × 100 = 28%.

∴ The correct answer is 28% Loss.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = 1000

Marked Price (MP) = 1200

Discount Percentage = 40%

Calculations:

⇒ Discount Amount = 40% of MP = (40 / 100) × 1200

⇒ Discount Amount = 480

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 1200 − 480 = 720

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 1000 − 720 = 280

⇒ Loss Percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = (280 / 1000) × 100 = 28%

∴ The correct answer is 28% Loss.

Additional Information

Relation between CP and MP

The formula linking Cost Price and Marked Price is MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%). In case of loss, use (100 − Loss%).

Net Percentage Change

Profit or Loss can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y / 100), where x is the Markup Percentage and y is the Discount Percentage (negative).

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which the Marked Price is higher than the Cost Price is given by: Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

questions.question: The marked price of a TV set is Rs.12,500. It sells with two successive discounts of 16% and 12%. An additional 5% discount is given on cash payment. What is the selling price of the TV set on cash payment?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of a TV set is Rs.12,500. It sells with two successive discounts of 16% and 12%. An additional 5% discount is given on cash payment. What is the selling price of the TV set on cash payment?
questions.solution:
Given:

MP = Rs. 12,500

D1% = 16%

D2% = 12%

D3% = 5%

Concept used:

SP of the TV.  = MP × (1 - D1%) × (1 - D2%) × (1 - D3%) 

Calculation:

⇒ SP of the TV. =  Rs. 12,500 × (21/25) × (22/25) × (19/20) 

⇒ 21 × 22 × 19

⇒  Rs. 8,778

Hence the correct answer is option 4).

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 45% above its cost price. The percentage of discount allowed to gain 16% is
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 45% above its cost price. The percentage of discount allowed to gain 16% is
questions.solution:
EXPLANATION &CALCULATIONS :

⇒ Let the cost price = Rs. 100

⇒ then, Marked price = Rs. 145

⇒ Required gain = 16%,

⇒ So Selling price = Rs 116

⇒ Discount = 145 - 116 = 29

⇒ Discount % = ( 29 / 145 ) × 100

⇒ 20%

∴ The percentage of discount allowed to gain 16 percent is 20%.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 550. It is sold for Rs. 428.45 after giving two successive discounts of 18% and x% on the marked price. What is the value of 2x?
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs. 550. It is sold for Rs. 428.45 after giving two successive discounts of 18% and x% on the marked price. What is the value of 2x?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price = Rs. 550

It is sold for Rs. 428.45 after giving two successive discounts of 18% and x% on the marked price. 

Concept used:

Selling price = Marked Price - Marked Price × Discount%

Calculation:

After giving the first 18% discount the price becomes

⇒ 550 - 550 × 18%

⇒ 550 - 99

⇒ Rs. 451

According to the question,

451 - 451 × x% = 428.45

⇒ 451 × x% = 451 - 428.45

⇒ 451 × x% = 22.55

⇒ x% = 22.55/451

⇒ x = 0.05 × 100

⇒ x = 5

Now, 2x = 2 × 5

⇒ 10

∴ The value of 2x is 10.

questions.question: A cloth store is offering "Buy 3, get 1 free". What is the net percentage discount being offered by the store?
questions.questionHtml: A cloth store is offering "Buy 3, get 1 free". What is the net percentage discount being offered by the store?
questions.solution:
Given:

A cloth store is offering "Buy 3, get 1 free".

Formula used:

Discount = \(\frac{MRP-SP}{MRP}\times 100\) 

Calculation:

Let the price of one cloth as 1Rs

selling price=price of 3 cloth=3Rs

Marked price=price of 4 cloths=4Rs

Discount = \(\frac{MRP-SP}{MRP}\times 100\)

⇒ \(\frac{4-3}{4}\times 100\)

⇒ \(\frac{1}{4}\times 100\) = 25%

Percentage discount offered is 25%.

questions.question: Under a discount scheme, a dozen pair of gloves quoted at ₹200 is available at a discount of 20%. How many pairs of gloves can be bought for ₹320?
questions.questionHtml: Under a discount scheme, a dozen pair of gloves quoted at ₹200 is available at a discount of 20%. How many pairs of gloves can be bought for ₹320?
questions.solution:
S.P of 12 pairs of gloves = \(\frac{100-20}{100}\) × 200 = \(\frac{80}{100}\) × 200 = Rs.160

In Rs. 160, 12 pairs can be bought

In Rs. 320, 24 pairs can be bought.
